title: Main street, twice
logline: 1997 on the left, 2021 on the right, joined at the center with no middle.

margin.note: ROFLCOPTER, tiny — the first time the name is lettered in his hand, spelled right.

panels.composition: One drawing. The main street of Small Wood from the top of the hill by the school: 1997 on the left half, 2021 on the right, joined at the center line with no seam. The mill's smokestack on the left becoming a cell mast on the right; a hardware store becoming an empty storefront becoming, very small, a skate shop's first sign; the same crow on the same seawall at both ends. Nobody in it. Then, on inspection: a seventeen-year-old in an overcoat far left, a man with a three-legged dog far right, walking toward each other and never meeting because the drawing has no middle.

characters.pose: far left, tiny, walking toward center
far right, tiny, walking toward center

props: hardware store → empty storefront → skate shop sign
the same crow on the seawall at both ends

image.prompt: a single full-page ink and soft watercolor drawing of a small coastal timber town's main street seen from the top of a hill, the left half as it was in the 1990s with a mill smokestack and a hardware store, the right half decades later with a cell mast and an empty storefront, joined seamlessly at the center, a crow on the seawall at both ends, and two tiny figures far apart walking toward the middle, muted ochre, slate and sea-foam, no panel borders
image.notes: The bird is not here yet. The crow is.

notes: The first private page. Signed with the reclaimed name.
